prompt: Senior public officials should be legally required to publish details of their income and property every year. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
planAr: المقدمة: أعد صياغة الفكرة وصرّح بموقفك (أوافق بشدة أو بتحفظ). الفقرة الأولى: حجة الشفافية والردع مع مثال (مقارنة الثروة بالراتب تكشف الإثراء غير المشروع). الفقرة الثانية: الرد على الاعتراضات (الخصوصية والأمن) مع حل وسط (نشر مع حماية البيانات الشخصية الحساسة). الخاتمة: أكّد موقفك.
ideas: Public officials are paid by taxpayers and should be accountable
Open records make illegal enrichment easier to detect
Journalists and citizens can compare wealth with salary
Privacy and safety concerns can be met by limited details
Honest officials have nothing to fear
Trust in institutions grows when rules apply to everyone

prompt: Some people believe that university education should be free for all students. Others think that students should pay for their own studies. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
planAr: المقدمة: اعرض الرأيين وأعلن نهجك. الفقرة الأولى: حجج التعليم المجاني (تكافؤ الفرص، حاجة الدولة إلى مهنيين) مع مثال. الفقرة الثانية: حجج دفع الرسوم (عبء الميزانية، الجدية والتحفيز) مع مثال. ثم رأيك (مثلا: مجاني مع نظام قروض أو منح). الخاتمة: لخّص.
ideas: Free tuition gives talented poor students a fair chance
Society benefits from more doctors, engineers and teachers
Public budgets are limited and universities need funding
Students who pay may take their studies more seriously
Grants and income-based loans can balance both sides

prompt: In many countries, public money is lost because officials accept bribes when awarding contracts for building projects. What are the causes of this problem, and what measures could be taken to solve it?
planAr: المقدمة: عرّف المشكلة وأعلن أنك ستعرض الأسباب ثم الحلول. الفقرة الأولى: الأسباب مع أمثلة (غياب الشفافية في المناقصات، تدني الرواتب، ضعف العقوبات). الفقرة الثانية: الحلول مع أمثلة (نشر بيانات العقود إلكترونيا، رقابة مستقلة، عقوبات رادعة، حماية المبلّغين). الخاتمة: اربط الحلول بالأسباب.
ideas: Secret tendering lets officials favour one company
Very low salaries can push clerks towards bribes
Weak punishment makes the risk seem small
Publishing contracts online allows public checking
Independent auditors should report to parliament
Whistleblowers need legal protection
model:
Corruption in public contracts drains billions from budgets that should pay for schools, roads and hospitals. This essay will examine the main causes and propose practical solutions.

One important cause is the lack of transparency in the way contracts are awarded. When tenders are decided behind closed doors, an official can favour a company that offers him a private payment, and nobody outside the room can see it. Low pay is a second cause. A clerk who earns barely enough to feed his family may see a bribe as the only way to survive, especially when everyone around him seems to do the same. Finally, weak punishment encourages the habit; if officials who are caught only lose their post and keep their wealth, the risk seems small compared with the reward.

Several measures could address these causes. First, governments should publish every stage of the tender online, including the list of bidders, the criteria and the final price. When citizens, journalists and rival companies can compare the figures, a suspiciously expensive bridge is much harder to hide. Some cities have already placed contract data on open websites, and local reporters have used them to question inflated costs.

Second, independent audit bodies should have the power to check projects and report directly to parliament, not to the ministers they are examining. Third, courts must apply real penalties, including prison and the return of stolen money, to officials and the companies that paid them. Fair salaries and protection for staff who report wrongdoing would also reduce the pressure to take part in it.

In conclusion, contract corruption grows where decisions are secret, salaries are low and punishment is weak. Open data, independent auditing, firm sentences and better protection for honest staff would together make bribery far more difficult and restore public trust.
notesAr: 1) البنية تطابق السؤال تماما: فقرة للأسباب وفقرتان للحلول، وكل حل مرتبط بسبب مذكور سابقا (الشفافية، الرواتب، العقوبات). 2) المثال المحسوس (جسر مكلف بشكل مشبوه، صحفيون محليون) يجعل الفكرة قابلة للتصور. 3) مفردات الموضوع دقيقة (tenders, audit bodies, return of stolen money) دون حشو.

prompt: Governments spend large sums of money on space exploration. Why do they do this? Do you think this money could be better spent on other things?
planAr: المقدمة: أعد صياغة الموضوع وأعلن أنك ستجيب عن السؤالين. الفقرة الأولى: لماذا تنفق الحكومات؟ (الاكتشافات العلمية، التقنيات المشتقة كالأقمار الاصطناعية، المكانة الوطنية) مع مثال. الفقرة الثانية: هل يمكن إنفاقه بشكل أفضل؟ قدّم رأيك مع مثال (الصحة والتعليم أولى، لكن بعض الإنفاق مبرر). الخاتمة: لخّص الإجابتين.
ideas: Space research leads to useful technology such as satellites
Weather forecasts and navigation depend on space systems
Countries want scientific prestige and cooperation
Hunger and disease are urgent problems on Earth
A small share of the budget can support both goals

prompt: Some courts are beginning to use computer programs to help judges review evidence and suggest sentences. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages?
planAr: المقدمة: أعد صياغة السؤال وحدد رأيك (مثلا: المزايا أكبر بشرط بقاء القرار بيد القاضي). الفقرة الأولى: المزايا مع مثال (السرعة، الاتساق في الأحكام، تقليل التحيز البشري). الفقرة الثانية: العيوب مع مثال (تحيز البيانات، غموض الخوارزمية، ضعف المساءلة) وكيف يمكن تقليلها. الخاتمة: لخّص موقفك.
ideas: Programs can review thousands of documents quickly
Consistent advice may reduce unfair differences between sentences
Data used to train a program may contain old bias
Defendants must be able to challenge how a result was reached
A human judge must stay responsible for the final decision

prompt: The main purpose of prison should be to prepare offenders for a useful life after release, not to punish them. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
planAr: المقدمة: أعد صياغة العبارة وصرّح بموقفك (أوافق إلى حد كبير). الفقرة الأولى: حجة التأهيل مع مثال (التدريب المهني يقلل العودة إلى الجريمة). الفقرة الثانية: الظروف القاسية لا تصلح الناس، ثم اعترف بدور العقوبة وفق الجرائم الخطيرة. الخاتمة: أكّد موقفك بصياغة جديدة.
ideas: Most prisoners return to society one day
Job training reduces reoffending
Harsh conditions can make people angrier
Loss of freedom is already a punishment
Dangerous offenders must be kept away from the public
model:
I agree to a large extent that prisons should concentrate on preparing offenders for life after release, although I do not think punishment can be ignored completely.

The strongest argument for rehabilitation is that most prisoners will eventually return to society. A man who serves five years for theft and leaves with no skills, no job and a criminal record is very likely to steal again. Prisons that offer education and training reduce this risk. For instance, an inmate who learns carpentry or computer repair can apply for a real job afterwards, and a steady salary gives him a reason to stay away from crime. Every person who does not reoffend means fewer victims and lower costs for the state, so rehabilitation protects the public better than long, empty sentences.

In addition, harsh conditions often make people angrier rather than wiser. Overcrowded cells and constant idleness can turn a minor offender into a bitter one. Programmes in which prisoners study, work and receive counselling for anger or addiction treat the causes of their behaviour instead of just locking it away. Several countries that have invested in such programmes report that fewer former prisoners return to custody.

However, I do not believe that punishment has no role. Losing one's freedom is itself a punishment, and it shows victims and the public that serious crimes have consequences. Dangerous offenders must also be kept apart from society for as long as they are a threat. Even so, prisons should offer them a way back.

In conclusion, the primary goal of imprisonment should be to change behaviour, because that is the surest way to make communities safer. Punishment through the loss of liberty is necessary, but it should be the starting point of a prisoner's journey back to society, not its final purpose.
notesAr: 1) الموقف مدروس: موافقة قوية مع تحفظ محدد (الجرائم الخطيرة)، وهذا أفضل من الموافقة المطلقة. 2) الحجة الأولى فيها سلسلة منطقية واضحة: مهارة، ثم وظيفة، ثم راتب، ثم ابتعاد عن الجريمة. 3) الخاتمة تعيد الفكرة بصياغة جديدة وصورة ختامية (بداية رحلة العودة) بدل تكرار الجمل.

prompt: Some people think that governments should do more to improve public health, for example by taxing unhealthy food. Others believe that people should take responsibility for their own health. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
planAr: المقدمة: اعرض الرأيين. الفقرة الأولى: دور الحكومة مع مثال (ضرائب على المشروبات المحلاة، قيود على الإعلانات، فحوص مجانية). الفقرة الثانية: مسؤولية الفرد مع مثال (الغذاء والرياضة قرارات شخصية، والتدخل قد يقيّد الحرية). ثم رأيك (توازن بين الاثنين). الخاتمة: لخّص.
ideas: Taxes on sugary drinks can reduce consumption
Poor families may lack healthy, affordable food
Public campaigns and clear food labels help people choose
Adults should be free to make personal choices
Healthy habits begin at home and in school

prompt: Huge amounts of plastic waste end up in rivers and seas around the world. What are the main causes of this problem, and what can governments and individuals do to reduce it?
planAr: المقدمة: وضّح خطورة المشكلة وأعلن البنية. الفقرة الأولى: الأسباب مع أمثلة (الاستخدام الواحد، ضعف جمع النفايات، التصريف من المصانع). الفقرة الثانية: ما تفعله الحكومات (حظر الأكياس، مسؤولية المنتجين، أنظمة إعادة التدوير) وما يفعله الأفراد (أكياس قابلة لإعادة الاستعمال). الخاتمة: لخّص.
ideas: Single-use packaging is cheap and everywhere
Poor waste collection lets rubbish blow into rivers
Fishing nets and factory waste add to the problem
Governments can ban or tax plastic bags
Producers should pay for collecting their packaging
Individuals can reuse bottles and bags

prompt: Many people share news stories online without checking whether they are true. Why do people do this? What can be done to reduce the spread of false information?
planAr: المقدمة: عرّف الظاهرة وأعلن أنك ستجيب عن السؤالين. الفقرة الأولى: لماذا يشارك الناس؟ (سهولة المشاركة، العاطفة، الثقة بالأصدقاء) مع مثال. الفقرة الثانية: الحلول مع مثال (التربية الإعلامية في المدارس، تعديل تصميم المنصات، نشر الحكومات معلومات دقيقة بسرعة). الخاتمة: لخّص الإجابتين.
ideas: One tap shares a message with hundreds of people
Shocking stories make us react before we think
We trust stories posted by friends and relatives
Schools can teach media literacy
Platforms could ask users to read before sharing
Reliable information must be published quickly
model:
People often forward startling stories within seconds of seeing them, and false information can travel across the world before experts have time to respond. There are clear reasons for this behaviour, and there are also practical ways to limit the damage.

Firstly, sharing is quick and costs nothing. A single tap sends a message to hundreds of friends, so people act on impulse without stopping to think. Secondly, emotional stories attract attention. A post that makes us angry or frightened feels urgent, and we want to warn others. Finally, many people trust a story simply because a relative or close friend posted it, and they assume that someone else has already checked it. For example, a false message claiming that a common medicine was dangerous was passed on by thousands of worried parents who only wanted to protect their children.

To tackle the problem, schools should teach media literacy from an early age. Pupils could practise checking who wrote an article, whether other reliable sources report the same facts and whether a photo has been used before. Adults who learn these habits are less likely to be misled. In addition, social media companies could add a short pause before a post is shared, asking users whether they have read the article. Small delays like this can reduce thoughtless sharing. Platforms should also label disputed claims clearly and make corrections easy to see.

Governments can play a part as well by publishing accurate information quickly and openly, so that rumours have less space to grow. However, they must avoid censorship, which can damage public trust.

In conclusion, false stories spread because sharing is effortless, emotion beats caution and people trust their friends. Education, better platform design and transparent public information together offer the best chance of slowing them down.
notesAr: 1) كل سؤال له إجابة منفصلة ومنظمة: ثلاثة أسباب (Firstly, Secondly, Finally) ثم حلول متعددة، فلا يضيع أي جزء من المطلوب. 2) المثال (رسالة كاذبة عن دواء ينشرها أولياء أمور قلقون) عاطفي وسهل الحفظ. 3) تنبيه ذكي في النهاية: الحل لا يجب أن يتحول إلى رقابة، وهذا يدل على تفكير ناقد.

prompt: As the world becomes more connected, traditional cultures and local languages are disappearing, and this is a harmful development. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
planAr: المقدمة: أعد صياغة الفكرة وبيّن موقفك. الفقرة الأولى: لماذا هو ضار؟ (فقدان الهوية والمعرفة التقليدية) مع مثال (لغة محلية لا ينطقها إلا كبار السن). الفقرة الثانية: الجانب الآخر (الثقافات تتغير دائما، والتواصل يفيد) مع مثال، ثم حلول (تعليم اللغات المحلية، التوثيق الرقمي). الخاتمة: أكّد موقفك.
ideas: Languages carry stories, medicine and local knowledge
Young people may prefer global brands and foreign languages
Cultures have always changed through contact
Technology can record songs, crafts and languages
Schools can teach local heritage
